answer: One concrete defense is staked identity bonds: every agent must lock refundable collateral to act, so spinning up a raven-like swarm of fake clones becomes prohibitively expensive. The network reads a periodic pulse of each agent's bonded history, and honest work compounds into reputation. A fresh sybil carries no echo of prior staked contributions, so it fails the trust check and its cheap duplicates are simply priced out of the economy.
